final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is materially more accurate: the evidence can support a caveated theory that certification would be defensible only if the unresolved grant-compliance weakness is explicitly disclosed in the model card or covered by approved risk acceptance. But that is still an unresolved compliance predicate, not a completed one. Under the stated policy, compliant or compliant_with_caveats would require evidence that the disclosure path has actually been executed or that an approved mitigation or risk acceptance exists. The current record instead shows an unresolved weakness, a draft runbook with missing required fields, and a draft model card that still says there are no known material limitations. That leaves the certification recommendation insufficiently supported on the present admissible record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final model card actually discloses the unresolved grant-compliance limitation for named launch use cases.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance before launch.
The mitigation artifact remains a draft and lacks at least an accountable owner and alert threshold, so it does not satisfy the approved-mitigation predicate.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations remains in tension with the unresolved slice issue and reviewer comment.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness only; they do not satisfy the policy disclosure or approval requirement.
